citation: Unknown photographer, Detail, Glessner House, ca. 1887. Andrew Dickson White Architectural Photograph Collection, Cornell University Library, accession15/5/3090.00156, ID10035009; catalog ss:3874294. The same exposure is reproduced as Cornell rear.jpg by Glessner House Museum.
author: Unknown photographer; Henry Hobson Richardson is the architect, not an attributed photographer
repository: Division of Rare and Manuscript Collections, Cornell University Library
locator: Northwest view of stable: both broad west lower lights and both upper slits, west gable, north portal, cupola and rear dormer. Prairie library audit104, a18-gh-cornell-glessner-rear-c1887.
rights_note: Cornell catalog viewed2026-10-15 explicitly states: The images in this collection are in the public domain and are believed to have no known U.S. copyright or other restrictions. Direct catalog-linked JSTOR IIIF image was downloaded and visually compared with the museum reproduction: same exposure, not independent corroboration. Credit Cornell University Library.
access_notes: Re-read2026-10-15 for owner-requested west-window positioning. Both direct Cornell scan and existing museum/library reproduction viewed; fixed west-plane diagnostic retains HABS wall length and declared eave reconstructions. The four opening centers are withheld from the fit.
what_it_supplies: Relative placement of the two upper slits and two broad lower west windows beneath the front gable
Original north stable portal and loft composition, roof intersection and cupola form at the photograph date
what_it_does_not_supply: An independently dimensioned west elevation or exact roof heights
1904 RGB colors, glazing reflectivity or later alterations
Independent corroboration of the museum reproduction of this same exposure
note: Ca.1887 is the catalog photograph date. West-wall homography gives a reconstructed horizontal check, not survey precision: retained eave assumptions and manual picks cause station uncertainty. No photo pixels become model textures.
